examples.en: In our country, winter is cold.
I introduced our country's food to a foreign friend.
The autumn sky in our country is clear.
In our country, we take off our shoes when entering a house.
Delivery in our country is fast.
People in our country eat tteokguk on Seollal.

explain: '한국'은 나라 이름이고, '우리나라'는 한국 사람이 자기 나라를 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요. '우리'가 들어 있어서 가까운 느낌이 있어요. '우리 나라'로 띄어 쓰지 않고 한 단어로 붙여 써요.

phrases.en: People in our country often eat kimchi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국 사람이 한국 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used by Koreans to talk about Korean people.

phrases.example: 우리나라의 봄은 꽃이 많이 피어서 예뻐요.
phrases.en: Spring in our country is pretty because many flowers bloom.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'를 붙여서 우리나라의 어떤 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '의' to talk about something of our country.

phrases.en: The highest mountain in our country is Hallasan.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에서'를 붙여 우리나라 안의 장소나 범위를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '에서' to refer to a place or range within our country.

explain_en: '한국' is the name of the country, while '우리나라' is what Koreans say when they talk about their own country. The word '우리' (our) gives it a close feeling. It is written as one word, not '우리 나라'.

examples.en: My little sibling knows all the days of the week.
At this restaurant the menu changes every day of the week.
What day of the week is the class?
I write the exam date and the day of the week.
My younger sibling doesn't know the names of the days yet.

explain: 요일 이름은 한자 뜻으로 기억하면 쉬워요. 월(달), 화(불), 수(물), 목(나무), 금(쇠), 토(흙), 일(해)이에요.

phrases.en: What day of the week is it today?
phrases.nuance_ko: 요일을 물을 때 가장 먼저 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The first phrase to use when asking about the day of the week.

phrases.en: The exercise is different every day of the week.
phrases.nuance_ko: ‘마다’를 붙이면 ‘요일 하나하나’라는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 마다 means each and every day of the week.

phrases.en: Do you know all the Korean names of the days?
phrases.nuance_ko: 월, 화, 수처럼 요일을 부르는 말을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when talking about the names of the days, like 월, 화, 수.

dict_examples.en: The volunteers take turns handling phone counseling on each day of the week.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: The day names are easy to remember through their Chinese-character meanings: 월 (moon), 화 (fire), 수 (water), 목 (wood), 금 (metal), 토 (earth), 일 (sun).

examples.en: The neighbor next door brought over some rice cakes.
I only exchange greetings with my neighbors.
Do you get along with your neighbors?
I returned the umbrella I borrowed from my neighbor.
At night I stay quiet out of consideration for my neighbors.
Our neighbor is a really kind person.

explain: 말할 때는 '이웃'이나 '이웃집 사람'이라고도 많이 해요. 아파트에서는 '옆집', '윗집', '아랫집'처럼 어디에 사는지 구체적으로 말하는 경우도 많아요.

phrases.en: The man next door and I are like family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가까이 살면서 정이 든 이웃을 사촌처럼 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Calls a neighbor you are close to a 'cousin' because you live so near and feel like family.

explain_en: Compound meaning a neighboring person; refers only to people, not places or countries (이웃사람과 친하다). In speech people often just say '이웃' or '이웃집 사람'. In apartment buildings people also often say '옆집' (next door), '윗집' (upstairs) or '아랫집' (downstairs) to be specific.

t90.ax: Do you get along with your neighbors?

examples.en: We are friends.
Let's go together!
Our school is in Seoul.

examples.ko: 우리 어디에서 만날까요? — 회사 앞에서 만나요.
examples.en: Where shall we meet? — Let's meet in front of the office.
Our team is working this weekend.
We work at the same company.

explain: 외동이어도 '우리 엄마', 혼자 살아도 '우리 집'이라고 해요. '내 엄마'라고 하면 어색해요. 한국어의 '우리'는 '나와 내 사람들'이라는 느낌이에요.

phrases.ko: 우리 사이에 뭘 이런 걸 다
phrases.example: 아이고, 우리 사이에 뭘 이런 걸 다 사 왔어요?
phrases.en: Oh, you didn't have to (said when receiving a gift from someone close)
phrases.nuance_ko: 선물을 받을 때 고마움을 겸손하게 표현
phrases.nuance_en: a modest way to show thanks when you receive a gift
phrases.en_equiv: Oh, you didn't have to (said when receiving a gift from someone close)

explain_en: Plain we/our, among peers and family (우리 엄마) Even an only child says 우리 엄마 ('our mom'), and someone living alone says 우리 집 ('our home'). 내 엄마 ('my mom') sounds odd. Korean 우리 has the feeling of 'me and my people'.

p.n: 저희 lowers the speaker's side, as when speaking to a superior.

examples.en: There are many patients today.
Where does this patient hurt?
The doctor sees a patient.
What is the patient's name?
I'm not the patient. I'm family.

explain: 병원 직원은 환자를 “환자분”이라고 불러요. “분”은 사람을 높이는 말이에요. 병원에서 “환자분!” 하고 부르면 바로 나를 부르는 거예요.

phrases.en: Sir/Ma'am (patient), please sit here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 환자를 높여 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in hospitals to politely call a patient.

phrases.en: The doctor sees a patient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의사가 환자를 진찰할 때 '보다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 보다 when a doctor examines a patient.

phrases.en: The patient's family waits here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 환자와 같이 온 가족을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the family members who come with a patient to the hospital.

explain_en: Hospital staff call a patient "환자분". "분" is a word that shows respect for a person. When someone at a hospital calls "환자분!", they are calling you.

examples.en: Are you a student?
Where are you going?
Where did you go yesterday?

explain: 주어일 때는 '너가'가 아니라 '네가'예요. 말할 때는 보통 [니가]라고 해요.

phrases.en: Everyone, without exception, laughed at the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누구나 모두
phrases.nuance_en: means everybody, with no exception
phrases.en_equiv: Everyone, without exception, laughed at the news.

examples.en: Today is the last class.
The last subway is at twelve.
Finally, do you have any questions?
The end of the drama is really sad.
Today is the last day of this sale.

explain: ‘마지막’의 반대말은 ‘처음’이에요. ‘처음부터 마지막까지’는 from start to finish예요.

phrases.en: Finally, there is something I want to say.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이나 순서의 끝에서 ‘finally’처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like 'finally' at the end of speech or a sequence.

phrases.en: Today is the last day of the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝나는 날을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the final day of something.

phrases.en: At the end, everyone clapped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일의 끝 부분을 말할 때 ‘에’를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 에 to talk about the end part of something.

gh: final; last stage of a process

p.n: The swap means the ultimate goal, not just the last one in a list.

examples.en: My uncle is a soldier.
Soldiers protect the country.
The soldiers walk in a line.
I met a soldier on the subway.

examples.ko: 저는 군인이 되고 싶어서 매일 운동해요.
examples.en: I want to become a soldier, so I exercise every day.
I'm grateful to the soldiers who protect the country.

explain: 사람은 '군인', 그 사람들이 있는 조직이나 곳은 '군대'예요. '군대에 가다'는 군인으로 지내러 간다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I want to become a soldier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업이나 꿈을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a job or dream.

phrases.en: My older brother went into the army.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군인이 있는 조직이나 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the organization or place where soldiers are.

phrases.en: A soldier showed me the way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이들이 군인을 친근하게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A friendly way children refer to a soldier.

explain_en: The person is a '군인', while the organization or place is '군대'. '군대에 가다' is often used for going away to serve as a soldier.

examples.en: One plus two is three.
Five plus five is ten.

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 더하기와 빼기를 배우고 있어요.
examples.en: My child is learning addition and subtraction.
Addition is easy, but division is hard.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 더하기 문제라서 금방 풀었어요.
examples.en: This was an addition problem, so I solved it quickly.
I drew a big plus sign on the board.

explain: '3 + 4'는 '삼 더하기 사'처럼 읽고, 숫자는 한자어(일, 이, 삼)로 말해요. 짝말은 '빼기, 곱하기, 나누기'예요. 계산기나 기호를 말할 때는 '플러스'도 쓰지만, 수학 시간에는 '더하기'가 기본이에요.

phrases.en: If you add two to three, it is five.
phrases.nuance_ko: '더하기'의 동사형으로, 계산하는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of '더하기', describing the act of adding.

phrases.en: Addition problems are easy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수학 숙제나 시험의 문제를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for math homework or test questions.

phrases.en: One plus one is two.
phrases.nuance_ko: '더하기'와 뜻이 같지만 말할 때 가볍게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '더하기' but used more casually when speaking.

explain_en: Spoken, school math; also read as 'plus' in sums (2 더하기 3) You read '3 + 4' as '삼 더하기 사', using Sino-Korean numbers (일, 이, 삼). Its partners are 빼기, 곱하기 and 나누기. '플러스' is also used for the sign or on a calculator, but in math class '더하기' is the basic word.
